title: PCA, kernel PCA, MDS, and manifold embeddings

items.title: Finite centering matrices and centered data
items.statement:
For an integer $n\ge1$, let $\mathbf1_n\in\mathbb R^n$ be the vector whose entries are all $1$, and let $I_n$ be the $n\times n$ identity matrix. The **centering matrix** is

$$H_n:=I_n-\frac1n\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T.$$

For $v\in\mathbb R^n$, write $\bar v:=n^{-1}\mathbf1_n^Tv$; then $H_nv=v-\bar v\mathbf1_n$. For a finite data matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with $p\ge1$, its **centered data matrix** is $X_c:=H_nX$; each column of $X_c$ has sum zero.

items.title: The maximum trace over q-dimensional orthonormal frames is the sum of the top q eigenvalues
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ be symmetric with eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_p$, counted with multiplicity. For $1\le q\le p$ and every $Q\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$ satisfying $Q^TQ=I_q$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(Q^TAQ)\le\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_j.$$

Equality is attained by taking the columns of $Q$ to be orthonormal eigenvectors for the $q$ largest eigenvalues. Equality holds exactly when the column space of $Q$ contains every eigenspace with eigenvalue greater than $\lambda_q$, is orthogonal to every eigenspace with eigenvalue less than $\lambda_q$, and uses a subspace of dimension $q-\#\{j:\lambda_j>\lambda_q\}$ from the eigenspace with eigenvalue $\lambda_q$.

items.title: Finite configurations with equal Gram matrices have isometric linear spans
items.statement: Let $n\ge0$, $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^d$, and $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathbb R^m$ be finite lists with $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle=\langle y_i,y_j\rangle$ for every $1\le i,j\le n$, using the standard Euclidean inner products. The assignment $\sum_{i=1}^n c_i x_i\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^n c_i y_i$ is a well-defined linear isometry from $\operatorname{span}\{x_i\}$ onto $\operatorname{span}\{y_i\}$; when $n=0$ both spans are zero spaces and the assignment is the unique zero map.

items.title: Deterministic finite nearest-neighbor lists and graph symmetrizations
items.statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^p$ with $n\ge2$, using the Euclidean norm $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{a=1}^p v_a^2)^{1/2}$. For $1\le k<n$, the deterministic $k$-nearest-neighbor list $N_k(i)$ consists of the first $k$ indices $j\ne i$ when the other indices are ordered by increasing pair $(\|x_i-x_j\|_2,j)$ lexicographically; thus equal distances are broken by increasing sample index. All graphs below have vertex set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The **union symmetrization** has edge $\{i,j\}$ when $j\in N_k(i)$ or $i\in N_k(j)$; the **mutual symmetrization** has edge $\{i,j\}$ exactly when both inclusions hold. Each included edge may be assigned weight $\|x_i-x_j\|_2$. For a radius $r>0$, the radius graph has edge $\{i,j\}$ exactly when $\|x_i-x_j\|_2\le r$ for $1\le i<j\le n$. An undirected graph is connected when every two vertices are joined by a finite edge path.

items.title: The finite centering matrix is the orthogonal projection onto the zero-sum subspace
items.statement: For $n\ge1$, let $H_n=I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T$. Then $H_n^T=H_n$, $H_n^2=H_n$, $H_n\mathbf1_n=0$, and for each $v\in\mathbb R^n$, $H_nv=v-(n^{-1}\mathbf1_n^Tv)\mathbf1_n$. Thus $H_n$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\mathbf1_n^Tv=0\}$.

items.title: Rank-q principal component analysis by Frobenius reconstruction error
items.statement:
For a finite data matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with $n,p\ge1$, set $H_n=I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T$ and $X_c=H_nX$. For an integer $q$ with $1\le q\le p$, a rank-$q$ PCA frame is a matrix $Q\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$ with $Q^TQ=I_q$. Its reconstruction is $X_cQQ^T$, and its squared Frobenius reconstruction error is

$$\|X_c-X_cQQ^T\|_F^2=\sum_{i<n}\sum_{j<p}(X_c-X_cQQ^T)_{ij}^2.$$

A rank-$q$ PCA solution is any frame minimizing this error over all such $Q$; its score matrix is $X_cQ$. A minimizing frame need not be unique when the relevant eigenvalues are tied.

items.title: Kernel principal component analysis for a finite positive-semidefinite Gram matrix
items.statement: Given $n\ge1$ data points and a finite symmetric Gram matrix $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ satisfying $a^TKa\ge0$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^n$, define $H_n=I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T$ and the centered Gram matrix $K_c=H_nKH_n$. The positive-semidefinite condition is an input hypothesis; no theorem that an arbitrary kernel formula produces such a matrix is assumed. For $1\le q\le n$, kernel PCA retains the $q$ largest eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\ge0$ of $K_c$ and associated orthonormal eigenvectors $u_1,\ldots,u_q$, returning the score matrix $U_q\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\lambda_1},\ldots,\sqrt{\lambda_q})$. Eigenvectors inside a tied eigenspace may be chosen arbitrarily.

items.title: Classical multidimensional scaling from a finite dissimilarity matrix
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric with nonnegative entries and zero diagonal, and write $D^{\circ2}$ for the matrix with entries $(D^{\circ2})_{ij}=D_{ij}^2$. Define $H_n=I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T$ and the centered matrix

$$B:=-\frac12H_nD^{\circ2}H_n.$$

For a requested dimension $q\ge1$, classical multidimensional scaling diagonalizes the real symmetric matrix $B$, retains up to the $q$ largest strictly positive eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ with orthonormal eigenvectors $u_j$, and returns coordinates whose columns are $u_j\sqrt{\lambda_j}$. If fewer than $q$ positive eigenvalues exist, it returns only those positive-eigenvalue coordinates. For non-Euclidean dissimilarities this is a spectral procedure; it does not assert exact recovery of all entries of $D$.

items.title: Minimum-norm affine reconstruction weights for a finite LLE neighborhood
items.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^p$, $n\ge2$, and $1\le k<n$. For each $i$, let $N_i$ be the first $k$ indices $j\ne i$ under the increasing lexicographic order of $(\|x_i-x_j\|_2,j)$, so equal distances are broken by sample index; the norm on $\mathbb R^p$ is $\|z\|_2=(\sum_{a=1}^p z_a^2)^{1/2}$. The local affine reconstruction weights are the vector $w_i=(w_{ij})_{j\in N_i}\in\mathbb R^k$ minimizing

$$\left\|x_i-\sum_{j\in N_i}w_{ij}x_j\right\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{j\in N_i}w_{ij}=1,$$

Among all minimizers, choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm $\|w_i\|_2=(\sum_{j\in N_i}w_{ij}^2)^{1/2}$. This minimum-norm rule fixes the weights even when the local covariance matrix is singular.

items.title: The top right singular subspace minimizes rank-q PCA Frobenius reconstruction error
items.statement:
Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, $n,p\ge1$, let $X_c=(I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T)X$, and let $1\le q\le p$. Write $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_p\ge0$ for the singular values of $X_c$, padding by zeros after its rank. Among all $Q\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$ with $Q^TQ=I_q$, the minimum of $\|X_c-X_cQQ^T\|_F^2$ is

$$\sum_{j=q+1}^{p}\sigma_j^2.$$

A frame is minimizing exactly when its column space contains every eigenspace of $X_c^TX_c$ with eigenvalue greater than $\sigma_q^2$, is orthogonal to every eigenspace with eigenvalue less than $\sigma_q^2$, and uses the remaining dimension inside the eigenspace with eigenvalue $\sigma_q^2$. In particular a choice of $q$ right singular vectors for the $q$ largest singular values is minimizing; ties can give different minimizing subspaces.

items.title: Double-centering a finite positive-semidefinite Gram matrix preserves positive semidefiniteness
items.statement: Let $n\ge1$ and let $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric and satisfy $a^TKa\ge0$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^n$. With $H_n=I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T$, the centered matrix $K_c=H_nKH_n$ is symmetric and positive semidefinite. Consequently it has an orthonormal eigenbasis and all its eigenvalues are nonnegative.

items.title: Double-centering Euclidean squared distances recovers their centered Gram matrix
items.statement: Let $n\ge1$. For every symmetric nonnegative zero-diagonal dissimilarity matrix $D$, the matrix $B=-\frac12H_nD^{\circ2}H_n$ used by classical multidimensional scaling is symmetric and has a real orthonormal eigendecomposition, though it may have negative eigenvalues. If $D_{ij}=\|z_i-z_j\|_2$ for points $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\mathbb R^d$, where $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{a=1}^d v_a^2)^{1/2}$, then $B=Z_cZ_c^T$ for the centered row-data matrix $Z_c=H_nZ$, so $B$ is positive semidefinite. The coordinates formed from all positive eigenvalues reproduce every pairwise distance exactly; if the requested embedding dimension is at least the number of positive eigenvalues, the truncated procedure is exact. The centered configurations obtained from $Z$ and these coordinates are related by a linear isometry between their spans, so the original configurations agree up to translation and Euclidean isometry of their affine spans.

items.title: Finite LLE affine least-squares weights have a unique minimum-norm minimizer
items.statement:
Fix $x_i\in\mathbb R^p$ and a nonempty finite neighbor list $N_i=(j_1,\ldots,j_k)$ of distinct indices. The constrained problem

$$\min_{w\in\mathbb R^k}\left\|x_i-\sum_{s=1}^k w_sx_{j_s}\right\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{s=1}^k w_s=1$$

has a nonempty affine set of minimizers, and exactly one member of that set has smallest Euclidean norm. Thus the minimum-norm rule in finite LLE defines one weight vector even when the local covariance matrix is singular. This conclusion uses no choice axiom.

items.title: Finite ISOMAP with deterministic neighborhoods and connected-graph shortest paths
items.statement: Input: a finite data matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with $n\ge2$, an embedding dimension $q\ge1$, and either a $k$-nearest-neighbor parameter $1\le k<n$ with an explicit union or mutual symmetrization choice, or a radius $r>0$. Use $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{a=1}^p v_a^2)^{1/2}$; for the $k$-nearest-neighbor option, each neighbor list orders candidates by increasing $(\|x_i-x_j\|_2,j)$, so equal distances are broken by sample index. Construct the selected undirected graph and give each edge $\{i,j\}$ weight $\|x_i-x_j\|_2$. If the graph is disconnected, return the status “disconnected” and do not claim finite all-pairs graph distances. If it is connected, define $d_G(i,j)$ as the minimum total edge weight over all paths from $i$ to $j$; because the graph is finite with nonnegative edge weights, a minimum occurs among its finitely many simple paths. Form the symmetric dissimilarity matrix $D_G=(d_G(i,j))$ and apply classical multidimensional scaling to $D_G$ with requested dimension $q$. This finite procedure makes no guarantee that graph distances accurately approximate manifold geodesics or that the output recovers a manifold.

items.title: Metric distance-stress multidimensional scaling
items.statement:
For a symmetric nonnegative zero-diagonal dissimilarity matrix $D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $n\ge2$, and a target dimension $q\ge1$, use the Euclidean norm $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{a=1}^q v_a^2)^{1/2}$. The **metric stress** of centered coordinates $Y=(y_1^T,\ldots,y_n^T)^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$, with $\mathbf1_n^TY=0$, is

$$S_D(Y):=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}\bigl(D_{ij}-\|y_i-y_j\|_2\bigr)^2.$$

Metric stress MDS is the separate optimization problem of minimizing $S_D(Y)$ over such centered $Y$. It is a distance-based, generally nonconvex objective and does not define the positive-eigenvalue solution used by classical multidimensional scaling; no solver convergence or global-optimizer guarantee is part of this definition.

items.title: Finite locally linear embedding with minimum-norm weights and a simple constant kernel
items.statement:
Input: a data matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with $n\ge2$, a neighbor count $1\le k<n$, and an output dimension $1\le q<n$, using $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{a=1}^p v_a^2)^{1/2}$. For every row point $x_i$, select the first $k$ other sample indices ordered by $(\|x_i-x_j\|_2,j)$ and use the minimum-Euclidean-norm affine least-squares weights on that neighborhood, with weights summing to $1$. Form $W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ by placing those weights in the selected columns of row $i$ and zeros elsewhere; every row of $W$ then sums to $1$. If $\ker(I_n-W)\ne\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1_n\}$, return the status “constant kernel not isolated” and do not specify an embedding. Otherwise put $M=(I_n-W)^T(I_n-W)$ and return any $Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$ minimizing

$$\operatorname{tr}(Y^TMY)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Y^T\mathbf1_n=0,\qquad Y^TY=I_q,$$

where $\operatorname{tr}$ is the sum of diagonal entries. Equivalently, take orthonormal eigenvectors for the $q$ smallest positive eigenvalues of $M$. Ties allow multiple outputs. This finite-matrix procedure makes no guarantee of manifold recovery or consistency.

items.title: Under the simple constant-kernel condition, LLE trace minimizers are bottom positive eigenvectors
items.statement: Let $W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ satisfy $W\mathbf1_n=\mathbf1_n$, put $M=(I_n-W)^T(I_n-W)$, and assume $\ker(I_n-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1_n\}$. Let $0<\mu_1\le\cdots\le\mu_{n-1}$ be the eigenvalues of $M$ restricted to the zero-sum subspace $\mathbf1_n^\perp$. For $1\le q<n$, the minimum of $\operatorname{tr}(Y^TMY)$ over $Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$ with $Y^T\mathbf1_n=0$ and $Y^TY=I_q$ is $\sum_{j=1}^q\mu_j$. The minimum is attained by taking the columns of $Y$ to be orthonormal eigenvectors for the $q$ smallest positive eigenvalues; when eigenvalues tie, the minimizing subspace may vary inside the tied eigenspace. The trace is the sum of diagonal entries.

title: PCA, kernel PCA, MDS, and manifold embeddings — Examples

items.title: A rank-one centered data matrix is reconstructed exactly by rank-one PCA
items.statement:
Let

$$X=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{3\times2},\qquad q=1.$$

The columns of $X$ already have mean zero and $X$ has rank one. The rank-one PCA frame $Q=(1,0)^T$ reconstructs $X$ exactly, so the minimum squared Frobenius reconstruction error is zero and the unique minimizing subspace is $\operatorname{span}\{(1,0)^T\}$.

items.title: A non-Euclidean three-point dissimilarity produces a negative MDS eigenvalue
items.statement:
Take the symmetric dissimilarity matrix

$$D=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&3\\1&3&0\end{pmatrix}.$$

It is nonnegative with zero diagonal and is not Euclidean because $D_{13}+D_{12}=2<D_{23}=3$. Its classical-MDS matrix $B=-\frac12H_3D^{\circ2}H_3$ has a negative eigenvalue, so positive-eigenvalue truncation is not exact distance recovery.

items.title: A one-nearest-neighbor graph can disconnect finite ISOMAP
A singular local LLE covariance still has a unique minimum-norm weight vector
items.statement: Take $x_1=0$, $x_2=1$, $x_3=-1$, and $x_4=0$ in $\mathbb R$, with $i=1$ and $k=3$. The neighbor order is $N_1=(4,2,3)$. Define the local difference matrix $Z_1=[x_1-x_j]_{j\in N_1}$ and its local covariance matrix $C_1=Z_1^TZ_1$; then $C_1$ has rank one and is singular. The affine reconstruction minimizers are $w_4=1-2t$, $w_2=w_3=t$ for real $t$, and the unique minimum-norm choice is $w_4=w_2=w_3=1/3$.

items.title: A connected LLE neighbor graph can have more than one fixed vector
Classical MDS, ISOMAP, and LLE give different embeddings of a four-point square
The metric stress objective is not convex even for two points
items.statement: Let two objects have dissimilarity $D_{12}=1$ and use one-dimensional centered coordinates $Y(t)=(t,-t)$, $t\in\mathbb R$. The metric stress is $f(t)=(1-2|t|)^2$, which is not convex: $f(0)=1$ while $\bigl(f(-1/4)+f(1/4)\bigr)/2=1/4$.
